title: Lighthouse AI - EdgeBurst latency economics discovery
summary: Initial technical discovery focused on meeting Lighthouse AI's low-latency streaming needs for edge-like inference. Discussed p95 goals, concurrency targets, fallback behavior, and security constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run a 2-week Dedicated pilot + benchmark, exchange security docs, and share a token/sec worksheet and initial config suggestions.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-30
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood), Daniel (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO), Ethan (Platform), Priya (SRE)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey folks thanks for squeezing us in, um this is Sofia from Redwood Inference.
[00:10] Maya: Hi Sofia, thanks, we wanted to focus on latency and streaming today — we've got this feature called EdgeBurst where customers expect very low p95 for short responses.
[00:20] Daniel: Great, could you give us the target p95 numbers and the concurrency shape?
[00:29] Maya: Sure, so goal is p95 around 150 to 250ms for short completion streams (approx 8-40 tokens). For longer generation it's okay to be higher, but interactive chat needs that p95.
[00:43] Ethan: To add, typical steady concurrency is 120 sessions, peaks up to 600 during promotions, and we sometimes see microbursts up to 1,200 for a few minutes.
[00:55] Priya: Security is a hard stop — we need VPC peering or Private deployment, and HSM/KMS integration for key management. Also SOC2 and audit logs.
[01:10] Sofia: Perfect, that helps. On the latency side there are a few levers — model choice, quantization, batching window, and whether you run Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. For p95 at 150ms we usually recommend Dedicated with pinned GPU capacity plus streaming-optimized kernels.
[01:30] Maya: We were hoping to evaluate Hosted first because of speed to market — but worried about predictable p95 during the bursts.
[01:38] Daniel: Hosted can work with routing/fallback policies, but reserved Dedicated gives you predictable tail latency. We can also set burst credits to handle spikes.
[01:48] Ethan: How does caching and KV cache affect streaming p95? We do prompt prefixes and long context reuse.
[01:55] Daniel: KV cache helps for repeated prefixes — it reduces token compute. But for very short bursts the scheduler and kernel warmup matter more. We also do prefix-level caching; if your prefix is stable across users you can save a lot of cycles.
[02:12] Maya: What's a realistic tokens/sec per session we should budget?
[02:16] Sofia: For streaming chat on an Llama2-like open model, a single session streaming at 30-80 tokens/sec is common. If you want 100+ tokens/sec consistently you'll need GPUs tuned for throughput and lower quantization quality may be required.
[02:32] Ethan: Our use is mostly short, 10-25 tokens responses but at high concurrency. So aggregate tokens/sec during peaks is important.
[02:40] Daniel: Right — so for math, 600 concurrent sessions at an average of 30 tokens/sec gives 18k tokens/sec sustained, bursts to 1200 sessions at 40 tps is 48k tokens/sec. Those are useful numbers for capacity planning.
[02:55] Priya: Do you support on-prem Private deployments? Air-gapped? We have customers who require air-gapped options.
[03:02] Sofia: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages. For air-gapped we'd need an enterprise engagement and some lead time — about 6-10 weeks for the on-prem installer/validation typically.
[03:15] Maya: Okay. For the Dedicated pilot we're thinking 2 weeks to run traffic and verify p95 targets. What's required from our side?
[03:24] Daniel: We'll need a sample prompt set, traffic distribution (histogram of session lengths and inter-arrival times), and a short test harness for streaming. We'll provide the load script.
[03:35] Ethan: Sounds good. Regarding fallback — if Dedicated is saturated, can Redwood route to a lower-tier hosted variant with graceful degradation?
[03:44] Daniel: Yes, we can set smart routing policies and automatic fallback to a smaller model or another region. It can be configured per route with latency/cost priorities.
[03:55] Maya: What's the expected difference in p95 between Dedicated and Hosted during a sustained peak?
[04:01] Sofia: Dedicated with reserved GPUs will keep p95 stable — maybe add 10-20ms variance for queuing. Hosted under multitenant bursts could see p95 inflation depending on load, potentially doubling in extreme congestions unless you have burst credits.
[04:19] Priya: About encryption — do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:23] Daniel: Yes; KMS/HSM integration is supported in Private and Dedicated. Hosted also supports CSEK for enterprise plans — there are nuances but we can send the security pack.
[04:34] Ethan: Can you walk through a sample benchmark config? We want to mimic our 20ms think-time between messages.
[04:41] Daniel: Absolutely. Our baseline script will replay your prompts with configurable think-time and stream behavior. For streaming p95 we capture token-level latencies and end-to-end response p95. We usually run a 30m steady-state plus 10m ramp and 5m burst.
[04:57] Maya: If we run that on Dedicated, what metrics will you share?
[05:00] Sofia: We'll provide p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batching stats, and per-token cost. Also cold-start times and kernel warmup traces if relevant.
[05:12] Ethan: What about multiplexing? We sometimes multiplex multiple user streams onto single session when prompts are tiny.
[05:19] Daniel: Multiplexing helps throughput but increases tail latency complexity. We can show a multiplexing config — often better for throughput-heavy workloads where p95 can be relaxed a bit.
[05:32] Maya: Our SLO is actually p95 200ms for interactive chat. If you can hit that with Dedicated that might be acceptable.
[05:39] Sofia: That’s achievable. We'll propose initial VM/GPU sizing — likely an A100-scale pool or similar with optimized kernels and quantized weights. We'll also test a smaller model variant as fallback to keep p95 in check during extreme load.
[05:55] Priya: On compliance, what audit logs do you provide? We need per-request logs, masking options, and retention control.
[06:03] Daniel: We can emit per-request trace IDs, redaction hooks, and configurable retention in the Console. For Private deployments you keep logs in your VPC. For Hosted, we provide long-term log retention as an add-on.
[06:16] Ethan: Any known gotchas with streaming and node-local caches? We've seen token duplications when reconnecting streams.
[06:24] Daniel: Reconnect logic needs idempotency tokens — we support resume tokens to avoid duplication, and we document best practices in the integration guide. There can be edge cases but they're manageable.
[06:36] Maya: Cost question — for Dedicated do you price per GPU-hour plus per-token or flat?
[06:42] Sofia: Dedicated is typically a reserved capacity contract: base monthly fee for the pool (GPU hours) plus per-token or per-output unit for overage. We'll send a clear matrix. Hosted is pure per-token tiers.
[06:55] Ethan: For the pilot, can we try a small Dedicated pool with a temporary burst allowance?
[07:00] Sofia: Yes — pilot pools with burst credits are common. We'll include that option in the proposal.
[07:08] Maya: Let's talk about quantization — we care about quality; half-precision vs 4-bit can affect latency and tokens/sec.
[07:15] Daniel: Right — 4-bit + special kernels yields big throughput gains but can regress on some instruction-heavy prompts. We can run A/Bs during the pilot: run 8-bit/4-bit and compare quality/regressions via your eval set. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profile per workload.
[07:35] Priya: Do you integrate with our existing telemetry (Datadog / Prometheus)?
[07:40] Sofia: Yes we emit Prometheus metrics and have Datadog hooks; Console also provides traces you can forward.
[07:47] Ethan: How long do kernels warm up after idle? Cold start concerns — during low-traffic nights we saw higher p95 in other services.
[07:55] Daniel: There's a warmup cost for models that have been paged out; with Dedicated you can keep a hot pool. We also do kernel prewarmed lanes for streaming to minimize warm starts.
[08:09] Maya: For our traffic shape, is it better to over-provision or rely on routing to fallback?
[08:14] Sofia: Both approaches work — Dedicated plus a small hosted fallback is the safest for SLOs. Overprovisioning keeps latency consistent but is costlier. We'll show cost estimates for several options.
[08:27] Ethan: Can you show an example of routing rules? E.g., latency-first for VIP users, cost-first for background jobs.
[08:33] Daniel: Yes — you can tag routes and set priorities: route A: latency-priority -> Dedicated pool in us-west; route B: cost-priority -> cheaper model or Hosted. We'll include example configs.
[08:47] Maya: Ok next question, what's realistic p99 on streaming? We care about p95 but p99 surprises are bad.
[08:54] Daniel: p99 is tougher — for well-provisioned Dedicated you might see p99 under 400-600ms for short streams; with Hosted multitenant it can spike to seconds under unusual congestion. We instrument retries and fallbacks for critical flows.
[09:10] Priya: Are there SLA credits if p95 misses?
[09:14] Sofia: For Dedicated enterprise SLAs yes, there are credits based on uptime/latency targets. Hosted has best-effort tiers, enterprise hosted plans can include stronger SLOs.
[09:25] Ethan: Any limitations on connection counts for streaming? TCP file descriptors, etc.
[09:30] Daniel: The platform supports large fanouts; for private deployments OS limits still apply but we provide recommended kernel tuning and a load-balancer pattern.
[09:42] Maya: For the pilot, can Redwood run a scripted 1,000 concurrent stream test for 10 minutes to validate p95 under burst?
[09:49] Sofia: Yes. We'll schedule that as part of the pilot test plan.
[09:53] Ethan: Great. On instrumentation, can you provide token-level timing? We want to see per-token latency distribution.
[09:59] Daniel: Yes, token-level traces are available in the Console and as exportable CSVs. We capture token generation times and batching windows.
[10:10] Maya: Let's talk numbers — can you give a back-of-the-envelope cost for sustaining 20k tokens/sec on Dedicated?
[10:18] Sofia: It depends on model, quant and GPU choice, but ballpark: a mid-size Dedicated pool might cost X depending on region; we'll provide a detailed estimate in the pricing sheet. (note: numbers omitted until we run pilot)
[10:30] Priya: We also need data residency for EU customers — do you support region pinning?
[10:34] Daniel: Yes, regional routing and model pinning exist. Private deployments let you keep everything in-region.
[10:41] Maya: Any recommendations for initial model variants? We care about safety and hallucination rates.
[10:46] Daniel: We'll propose 2 variants: a higher-quality medium-sized model for VIP routes and a lower-latency quantized variant as fallback. We'll run evals on your prompt set to measure regressions.
[10:58] Ethan: Regarding logs, do you provide anonymization hooks before logs leave our VPC?
[11:03] Sofia: Yes for Private implants you can configure pre-shipping redaction. Hosted supports PII redaction with patterns and custom hooks.
[11:12] Maya: Ok, let's recap actions and timeline.
[11:16] Sofia: Recap: Redwood to send benchmark worksheet and load script; customer to send prompts and traffic histogram; Redwood to scope a 2-week Dedicated pilot with burst credits; security docs exchanged and SRE to review.
[11:31] Maya: That sounds right. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[11:34] Daniel: No blockers; we'll need a technical contact (Ethan) and an SRE contact (Priya) for the pilot.
[11:41] Ethan: I'll be point for the traffic and test harness. Priya will sign off on security.
[11:47] Priya: Yep. Also, please include notes about replaying session resume tokens; we want to avoid duplication edge cases.
[11:55] Daniel: Will do.
[12:00] Sofia: I'll email the worksheet and a proposed pilot contract tomorrow.
[12:05] Maya: Great, thanks everyone.
[12:07] Sofia: Thanks all, talk soon.

[End of transcript]
